title: commit-check
description:
Configuration for commit-check, a commit message, branch naming, and push linter
https://commit-check.com/configuration/

inherit_from.description:
Inherit configuration from a parent file, whose settings this file overrides. Supports github: shorthand (e.g., github:owner/repo:path/to/cchk.toml or github:owner/repo@ref:path/to/cchk.toml), an HTTPS URL, or a local file path. Only one level is followed.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#inheriting-a-shared-config

warn.description:
Checks or rule IDs (in any case) to report without failing the run, e.g. ["branch", "CC003"]. A name that matches no rule is a configuration error.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#report-a-rule-without-enforcing-it

anyOf.description: A single check or rule ID.

message_pattern.description:
Custom regex pattern for commit message validation. When set (non-empty), this replaces the auto-generated Conventional Commits regex entirely. Useful for enforcing custom formats such as JIRA smart commits (e.g., ^PROJ-\d+: .+).
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc001

subject_capitalized.description:
Subject must start with a capital letter.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc002

subject_imperative.description:
Subject must be in imperative mood.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc003

subject_max_length.description:
Maximum length of the subject line, not counting the " (#123)" a GitHub squash merge adds. Commits by dependabot[bot] and renovate[bot] skip it. 0 turns the check off.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc004

subject_min_length.description:
Minimum length of the subject line, not counting the " (#123)" a GitHub squash merge adds. Commits by dependabot[bot] and renovate[bot] skip it. 0 turns the check off.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc005

allow_commit_types.description:
Allowed commit types when conventional_commits is true.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc001

allow_revert_commits.description:
Allow the Revert "..." and Reapply "..." commits git revert writes.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc007

allow_fixup_commits.description:
Allow fixup commits: fixup!, squash! and amend! subjects.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc009

allow_wip_commits.description:
Allow work-in-progress commits (e.g., WIP: <commit message>).
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc010

require_body.description:
Require a body in the commit message.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc011

body_max_line_length.description:
Maximum length of a body line. Lines with a URL, a single word with no space (a path, a hash) and the trailer block are not counted, and commits by dependabot[bot] and renovate[bot] skip it. 0 turns the check off.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc018

require_signed_off_by.description:
Require Signed-off-by line in the commit message footer.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc012

ignore_authors.description:
List of commit authors or co-authors (Co-authored-by: lines) to bypass all commit checks. Useful for bots (e.g., dependabot[bot], coderabbitai[bot]).
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#commit

author_email_pattern.description:
Custom regex for the author email check (--author-email).
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc102

author_name_pattern.description:
Custom regex for the author name check (--author-name). When empty, the built-in default pattern is used.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc101

ai_attribution.description:
AI attribution policy. "forbid" rejects any commit carrying AI attribution (CC013). "disclose" accepts AI assistance disclosed with one of ai_disclosure_trailers (CC014) and rejects the tool as a co-author (CC015) or sign-off (CC016). "ignore" disables the check.
https://commit-check.com/guides/policies/#ai-attribution

ai_disclosure_trailers.description:
The trailers that disclose AI assistance when ai_attribution is "disclose". The first one is what a correction is written with. Signed-off-by is refused.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc014

ai_disclosure_pattern.description:
A regex the disclosure trailer's value must match when ai_attribution is "disclose", e.g. ^\S+/\S+$ for an agent/model format. Empty accepts any value.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc014

require_verified.description:
GitHub App only. Every commit has to show Verified on GitHub. The CLI and the Action do not check signatures.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#verified-commits

require_description_grammar.description:
Also hold the description after <type>/ to the Conventional Branch grammar: lowercase letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens, dots only inside a word.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc201

allow_branch_types.description:
Allowed branch types when conventional_branch is true. The default is a superset of the Conventional Branch spec's types.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc201

allow_branch_names.description:
Additional standalone branch names allowed when conventional_branch is true (e.g., ["staging", "production"]). main, master, develop, HEAD, PR-* and gh-readonly-queue/* are always allowed.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc201

require_rebase_target.description:
Target branch for rebase requirement. If not set, no rebase validation is performed.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc202

ignore_authors.description:
List of authors to bypass branch checks.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#branch

allow_force_push.description:
Allow force pushes. Set to false to block force pushes when used as a pre-push hook or with --no-force-push.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc301

regex.description:
Pattern a tag name must match. The default is the official SemVer pattern with an optional leading v. An empty value disables the pattern match.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc401

files.title: File rules
files.description:
Settings for the committed files checks.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#files

max_size.description:
Largest a committed file may be, in bytes or with a B, KB, MB or GB suffix (binary units, so 5MB is 5 x 1024^2). Empty disables the rule.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc302

prohibited_patterns.description:
fnmatch patterns a committed path may not match, e.g. ["*.pem", ".env", "id_rsa*"]. A bare pattern also matches the file name at any depth. Empty disables the rule.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc303

max_path_length.description:
Longest a committed file path may be, in characters. 0 disables the rule.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc304

pull_request.title: Pull request rules
pull_request.description:
Settings for pull requests, read by the GitHub App and, for ai_declaration_checkboxes, by the CLI and the Action.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#pull_request

check.description:
GitHub App only. "commits" checks every commit of a pull request on its own; "squash" checks the one message a squash merge would land.
https://commit-check.com/configuration/#pull-requests-every-commit-or-the-squash-message

ai_declaration_checkboxes.description:
The texts of the AI declaration boxes in the pull request template, one per box. When set, a pull request description must tick exactly one of them.
https://commit-check.com/rules/#cc501

body_ai_attribution.description:
GitHub App only. Check the pull request description against the AI rules (CC013 to CC016), and its AI declaration boxes when ai_declaration_checkboxes is set.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#ai-written-pull-requests

ai_label.description:
GitHub App only. Label a pull request an AI tool wrote any of: true for the ai-assisted label, or the label's name. Labels are only added, never removed.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#ai-written-pull-requests

jira.title: Jira rules
jira.description:
GitHub App only; the CLI and the Action ignore this section.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#jira-ticket-references

required.description:
Every commit message, or the squash message, has to reference a Jira ticket.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#jira-ticket-references

pattern.description:
Regex for a ticket reference, e.g. PROJ-\d+ for one project.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#jira-ticket-references

suggestion.description:
The fix shown when the reference is missing. Empty uses the built-in text.
https://commit-check.com/guides/github-app/#jira-ticket-references
